verses.text: One day Dinah, the daughter Leah had given Jacob, went out to visit the young women of the land.
Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, who ruled that area, saw her. He took her and forced her to sleep with him, and he disgraced her.
But his heart was drawn to Dinah, Jacob's daughter. He loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her.
Shechem said to his father Hamor, "Get me this girl as my wife."
Jacob heard that his daughter Dinah had been disgraced. But his sons were out in the fields with his livestock, so he said nothing about it until they came home.
Then Shechem's father Hamor went out to talk with Jacob.

Meanwhile, Jacob's sons had come in from the fields as soon as they heard what had happened. They were shocked and furious, because Shechem had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by sleeping with Jacob's daughter. Such a thing should never be done.
But Hamor said to them, "My son Shechem has his heart set on your daughter. Please let him marry her.
Let our families marry each other. Give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.
You can live among us, and the land will be open to you. Live in it, trade in it, and buy property in it."
Then Shechem said to Dinah's father and brothers, "Please be kind to me, and I will give you whatever you ask.
Make the bride price and the gift as great as you like, and I will pay whatever you ask me. Only let me marry the girl."
Because Shechem had disgraced their sister Dinah, Jacob's sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor with a trick.
They said to them, "We cannot do such a thing. We cannot give our sister to a man who is not circumcised. That would be a disgrace to us.
We will agree to it on one condition only: that you become like us by circumcising all your males.
Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will live among you and become one people with you.
But if you will not agree to be circumcised, we will take our sister and go."
Their offer seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.
The young man did not waste any time doing what they said, because he was delighted with Jacob's daughter. And he was the most respected member of his father's family.
So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city to speak to the men of their city.
They said, "These men are friendly towards us. Let them live in our land and trade in it. The land has plenty of room for them. We can marry their daughters, and they can marry ours.
But the men will agree to live with us as one people only on one condition: that every male among us is circumcised, as they are.
Will not their livestock, their property and all their other animals become ours? So let's agree to their condition, and they will settle among us."
All the men who went out of the city gate agreed with Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male in the city was circumcised.

Three days later, while all of them were still in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, who were Dinah's brothers, took their swords. They attacked the city, which was not expecting it, and killed every male.
They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the sword, took Dinah from Shechem's house and left.
Then the other sons of Jacob came upon the dead bodies and looted the city where their sister had been disgraced.
They took their sheep, cattle and donkeys, and everything else of theirs in the city and in the fields.
They carried off all their wealth and all their women and children, and took everything in their houses.

Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have brought trouble on me. You have made me hated by the people living in this land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. We are only a few, and if they join together against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed."
But they replied, "Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?"
